_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: The public funding explainer now reads the model instead of copies of it. Its priority descriptions, the baseline requirements a college has to meet, and the participation deadline had all been typed onto the page by hand, and each had quietly drifted from what the model actually says — one card was describing a measure we stopped using. The page also gained a Download PDF button, a section that puts the three priorities and the milestone dates together, section titles in the model's own words, and a college table that fits the window. Separately, the test suite went red on main with nobody's hands on it: three checks had memorised figures that the nightly data refresh recomputes, so an ordinary data update broke them and cost another piece of work an hour proving it was not at fault. Those checks now read the figures rather than remembering them. Main is green.

items.text: One thing from the 15 September decision sheet is yours: a note to MAP about the Dashboard's "Eligible" label, which actually shows applied credit. It is drafted and waiting for you to send at docs/map_eligible_label_note_draft.md — check the figures again first, because the reconciliation is the whole argument.

When the origination data lands, half of it works by itself and half does not. The noncredit location side switches on automatically. The landing page / portal / batch upload side waits for a deliberate one-line change, made only once the exact spellings are confirmed, and the only signal that it is waiting is a line in a daily log. Worth giving that to someone by name.

Make the origination cutover the moment MAP ships the Origin column: read the origin_values histogram the daily build emits, confirm the spellings, then switch the portal measure from the Potential Student stand-in to the named origins. Only that makes Priority 1's three-route label true and gives it real units.
Carry Counselor_Verified into the daily fetch column list so the counselor measure cannot quietly stop being emitted.

Put the assistant's sign-in awareness live: dispatch the cpl-chat deploy workflow. What changes: nothing for the public page, the Fact Sheet drawer, map.rccd.edu or the vendor iframe. On COBI, a signed-in reviewer or team-phrase holder sees one line under the assistant saying it recognized the sign-in — the proof that the server, not the page, decided who is asking. The log also records who asked and from where. The database change is already in place, so the order does not matter. Then try it: sign in, ask one question on the CPL Assistant tab, look for the line.

Say go on the hourly health probe, or make the one-line change yourself. Its own notes say to raise it from every three hours to hourly once billing moved to the corporate account, which happened on 10 September; the remote session that tried to make the change was stopped by its permission rules because a scheduled workflow is a shared resource that spends real funding (about $22 a month at the notes' estimate). The change is the cron line in cpl-chat-health.yml: '7 */3 * * *' becomes '7 * * * *'.

Forward the KYND memo (vault: 20260911_Memo_map_rccd_edu_WordPress_wp2shell_Notice.docx) to whoever holds the SiteGround login for map.rccd.edu, filling in the TO line. Two things come back: the WordPress version on both the production site and staging2.map.rccd.edu, which the notice did not list, and whether the log search found anything. Then answer KYND. Until the site is confirmed clean, the Monday job that copies the site's story cards onto the Fact Sheet keeps running; pausing it is your call, and the current cards checked clean.

The statewide course descriptions you want a C-ID course to inherit are not in our data. You thought they came with the TMC tab work — that work gave us the 293 C-ID codes, which is probably what you are remembering, but not a word of the descriptive text behind them. So the ask to ASCCC is narrower than it looked: we have the identifiers and need only the descriptor prose.

Six observations from the full sweep of SkyView are still open for your read. You have already ruled on one of them: the check boxes stay for now, because people cannot know what is available unless the list is in front of them. The rest are waiting.

DR-24 is a governance row with an owner and no surface yet: an added skill lands as proposed with the reviewer's name and the day, and joins the published outline when a second curator agrees; a removal works the same way in reverse. Building that means the map's first write, so it routes through Governance and the privacy review first.

After Sam's deploy, read the new log columns: how many turns came from a signed-in reviewer, how many from the team phrase, how many from the public, and from which surface. The count of six real questions in thirty hours could not tell the COBI tabs from the public page; now it can. Also show those two columns in Sierra Training's conversation list, which reads the same table.

Build the floating assistant bubble on every COBI tab — Sam's ask from the 11th. The flag it needed exists now; the control does not. It mounts the same assistant the CPL Assistant tab uses, in the house style, with controls at least 24 pixels tall and a single column on a phone. What a signed-in reader may additionally see is a separate decision that goes through Governance first.
